shloka: तपःस्वाध्यायनिरतं तपस्वी वाग्विदां वरम्। नारदं परिपप्रच्छ वाल्मीकिर्मुनिपुङ्गवम्॥
translation: Valmiki, the ascetic, asked Narada, the preeminent among the learned, who is always absorbed in penance and self-study.

shloka: कोऽन्वस्मिन्साम्प्रतं लोके गुणवान् कश्च वीर्यवान्। धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च सत्यवाक्यो दृढव्रतः॥
translation: Who is that person in this world today, endowed with good qualities, valorous, knowing dharma, grateful, truthful, and firm in his vows?

shloka: गच्छता मातुलकुलं भरतेन तदाऽनघः। शत्रुघ्नो नित्यशत्रुघ्नो नीतः प्रीतिपुरस्कृतः॥
translation: When Bharata went to his maternal uncle's house, the sinless Shatrughna, the destroyer of his eternal enemies (passions), was also taken along with him out of love.
